3. Complaint acknowledgement and response times
Aurora Bank will acknowledge complaints promptly. Where possible, we resolve simple complaints within three business days. More complex complaints may take longer.
Indicative response standards:
| Complaint type | Expected handling |
|---|---|
| Simple service issue | Aim to resolve within 3 business days. |
| Standard complaint | Written final response normally within 15 business days for payment-service complaints, or within 30 calendar days for other complaints where local rules allow. |

Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment
13. Payment holidays and hardship support
Aurora Bank may offer temporary support if a customer is experiencing financial difficulty. Support can include payment deferral, temporary reduced payments, interest-only periods, debt advice referral, breathing-space arrangements, or restructuring.
Support is not automatic and may affect credit records, total interest, product eligibility, or future borrowing. Customers should provide accurate information about income, expenses, assets, debts, and the cause of difficulty.
Vulnerable-customer support is described in [Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility](10_complaints_vulnerable_customers_and_accessibility.md).

13. Fee disputes
Customers who believe a fee was charged incorrectly should contact Aurora Bank with the transaction date, amount, account, and reason for dispute. Fees caused by bank error will be refunded. retrieved_chunks.content:
Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
8. Scams and authorized push payment fraud
A scam payment occurs when a customer is tricked into authorizing a payment. Examples include impersonation scams, investment scams, romance scams, invoice redirection, purchase scams, and safe-account scams.
Aurora Bank will review scam reports and may attempt recovery from the receiving bank. Refund outcomes depend on law, scheme rules, customer conduct, warning effectiveness, and whether funds remain recoverable. Customers should report immediately and preserve evidence such as messages, phone numbers, websites, invoices, and payment instructions.
If a customer is currently speaking to a suspected scammer, they should end the call or chat and contact Aurora Bank using a known channel, not a number provided by the caller.

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
6. Time limits
Customers should raise disputes promptly. Card-scheme time limits can be short and may run from transaction date, expected delivery date, cancellation date, or merchant promise date.
Indicative timeframes:
| Claim type | Customer should report by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Immediately, and no later than 13 months where legal rules permit | Faster reporting can reduce loss. |
| Goods or services not received | After expected delivery date, usually within 120 days of expected receipt | Scheme rules vary. |
| Refund not processed | After merchant’s refund timeframe, usually within 120 days of refund promise | Evidence needed. |
| ATM cash not dispensed | Within 30 days if possible | ATM balancing may be time-sensitive. |

8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments
Direct debits are authorized by the customer to allow a payee to collect variable or fixed amounts. Standing orders are instructions created by the customer to pay a fixed amount on a schedule. Recurring card payments are card-authorized merchant arrangements and are not the same as direct debits.
Cancellation rules differ:
- A standing order can normally be cancelled in online banking before the processing cutoff.
- A direct debit can be cancelled with Aurora Bank, but the customer should also cancel the agreement with the merchant.
- A recurring card payment should be cancelled with the merchant. Aurora Bank can block future merchant attempts in some cases, but this may not cancel the underlying contract.
Payment execution and cancellation timings are described in [Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times](03_payments_transfers_and_cutoff_times.md).

10. Open banking
Open banking allows a customer to give a regulated third-party provider access to account information or payment initiation services. Aurora Bank will provide access only after the customer gives permission through the required secure process.
Important open banking points:
- Aurora Bank will never ask the customer to share online banking passwords with a third-party provider.
- The customer can withdraw open banking consent through Aurora online banking or the third-party provider.
- Revoking access does not delete data already received by the third-party provider.
- The third-party provider is responsible for its own use of data after it receives it.
- Payment initiation through open banking may still require strong customer authentication.
Customers should use only regulated providers and should check the provider name carefully before approving access.

6. Overdraft basics
An arranged overdraft is a credit facility attached to a current account. It allows the balance to go below zero up to an approved limit. | Payment type | Typical use | Typical currency | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEPA Credit Transfer | Standard euro transfer within SEPA | EUR | Normally arrives by the next business day after execution. |
| SEPA Instant Credit Transfer | Fast euro transfer within participating banks | EUR | Usually processed within seconds, subject to limits and screening. |
| Internal transfer | Transfer between Aurora Bank accounts | EUR or account currency | Usually immediate unless held for checks. |
| Standing order | Repeating customer-initiated payment | EUR | Customer controls amount, recipient, and schedule. |
| Direct debit | Merchant or organization collects payment after customer authorization | EUR | Customer can cancel mandate; merchant contract may remain. |
| International wire | Cross-border transfer outside SEPA or in non-euro currency | Multiple | Additional information, fees, FX spread, and correspondent banks may apply. |
| Card payment | Purchase or withdrawal using debit or credit card | Multiple | Authorization and final settlement may differ. |
Not all payment types are available on youth, savings, basic, or restricted accounts.

Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange
8. Current account interest
Aurora Everyday Current Account and Basic Payment Account do not normally pay credit interest. Promotional or packaged accounts may pay interest on balances up to a stated cap. Interest eligibility can depend on minimum monthly deposits, direct debit activity, product package, or residency.

Current & Savings Accounts Terms
6. Overdraft basics
An arranged overdraft is a credit facility attached to a current account. It allows the balance to go below zero up to an approved limit. Arranged overdrafts are subject to credit assessment and are not guaranteed. Details are in [Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment](05_loans_overdrafts_and_credit_assessment.md).
An unarranged overdraft occurs when the account goes below zero without approval or exceeds an arranged limit. Aurora Bank may refuse payments that would create or increase an unarranged overdraft. Fees and interest may apply as described in [Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange](06_fees_interest_and_exchange_rates.md).
Youth accounts, Basic Payment Accounts, savings accounts, and Fixed Term Deposits do not offer arranged overdrafts.

8. Youth accounts and accounts for minors
A Youth Current Account is available to customers aged 15 to 17 with guardian consent. The guardian must verify their identity and relationship to the minor. Youth accounts do not offer overdrafts, credit cards, cheque facilities, or high-value international payments.
When the customer turns 18, Aurora Bank may convert the account to an adult account after providing notice. The customer may need to provide updated identity, tax residency, and address information.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
6. Payment authentication
Payments may require strong customer authentication. Authentication can include a password, app confirmation, biometric confirmation, one-time passcode, hardware token, or call-back verification. Aurora Bank will never ask a customer to disclose a full password, full card PIN, or remote-access code.
Additional security checks may delay a payment. Aurora Bank may hold or reject a payment if fraud, sanctions, money laundering, scam, account takeover, or unusual activity indicators are present.

Packaged accounts may include non-banking benefits, enhanced service channels, higher ATM fee allowances, or travel-related features. Benefits may be provided by third parties and may have separate eligibility terms.

Aurora Bank uses layered security controls to protect accounts. These controls may include encryption, device binding, login monitoring, fraud scoring, strong customer authentication, payment warnings, transaction limits, account locks, and manual review.
Security controls may occasionally delay payments, block card use, restrict online access, or require additional verification. Aurora Bank will not compensate for inconvenience where a control was applied reasonably for safety or legal compliance.

We normally accept one of the following:

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
2. Strong customer authentication
Strong customer authentication uses at least two independent elements from the following categories:
- something the customer knows, such as password or PIN;
- something the customer has, such as registered device or hardware token;
- something the customer is, such as fingerprint or facial recognition.
Some low-risk transactions may be exempt, but Aurora Bank may still require authentication based on fraud risk, transaction amount, merchant type, new device, new payee, unusual behavior, or regulatory rules.

Current & Savings Accounts Terms
8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments
Direct debits are authorized by the customer to allow a payee to collect variable or fixed amounts. Standing orders are instructions created by the customer to pay a fixed amount on a schedule. Recurring card payments are card-authorized merchant arrangements and are not the same as direct debits.
Cancellation rules differ:
- A standing order can normally be cancelled in online banking before the processing cutoff.
- A direct debit can be cancelled with Aurora Bank, but the customer should also cancel the agreement with the merchant.
- A recurring card payment should be cancelled with the merchant. Aurora Bank can block future merchant attempts in some cases, but this may not cancel the underlying contract.
Payment execution and cancellation timings are described in [Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times](03_payments_transfers_and_cutoff_times.md).

1. Card types
Aurora Bank may issue the following card types:
| Card type | Linked to | Main purpose | Key restrictions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Debit card | Current account | Spending the customer’s own available funds | No borrowing unless an overdraft is available. |
| Youth debit card | Youth current account | Controlled spending for customers aged 15 to 17 | Lower limits; no gambling merchants; guardian controls may apply. |
| Credit card | Separate credit-card account | Borrowing up to approved credit limit | Interest, minimum payments, and credit checks apply. |
| Virtual card | Current or credit-card account | Online and mobile wallet payments | May not support ATM cash withdrawal. |
| Replacement card | Existing card account | Replaces lost, stolen, damaged, or expired card | Old card may be cancelled when replacement is issued. |
A card remains property of Aurora Bank and must be returned or destroyed on request.

Aurora Bank may offer temporary support if a customer is experiencing financial difficulty. Support can include payment deferral, temporary reduced payments, interest-only periods, debt advice referral, breathing-space arrangements, or restructuring.

Aurora Bank may provide general support through social media but will not conduct full account servicing through public comments. Customers should not post account numbers, card numbers, personal documents, transaction details, or complaint evidence publicly.

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
11. Domestic abuse and financial abuse
Aurora Bank recognizes that financial abuse can include controlling access to money, coercing loans, intercepting cards, monitoring statements, forcing transfers, or misusing joint accounts.
Customers can request confidential support. Aurora Bank can discuss safe contact methods, correspondence suppression, card replacement, account separation options, payment controls, and referral to specialist organizations. Joint account changes may require legal or operational safeguards.

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
8. Third-party authority and support persons
A customer can ask Aurora Bank to communicate with a support person. The level of access depends on authority provided:
| Authority type | What it usually allows |
|---|---|
| Trusted contact | Aurora Bank may contact the person if concerned about customer welfare or financial harm; no transaction authority. |
| One-time verbal authority | Discussion of a specific matter during a call or appointment. |
| Third-party mandate | Ongoing account discussion or limited account operation, depending on mandate. |
| Power of attorney | Legal authority according to the document and local law. |
| Guardian or court-appointed representative | Authority defined by court or law. |
Power of attorney and estates processes are described in [Account Closure, Inactivity, Estates & Power of Attorney](11_account_closure_inactivity_estates_and_power_of_attorney.md).

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
3. Complaint acknowledgement and response times
Aurora Bank will acknowledge complaints promptly. Where possible, we resolve simple complaints within three business days. More complex complaints may take longer.
Indicative response standards:
| Complaint type | Expected handling |
|---|---|
| Simple service issue | Aim to resolve within 3 business days. |
| Standard complaint | Written final response normally within 15 business days for payment-service complaints, or within 30 calendar days for other complaints where local rules allow. |
| Complex complaint | If more time is needed, Aurora Bank will explain the delay and provide a final response within the maximum period required by law. |
| Fraud, chargeback, or scam complaint | Investigation timelines depend on scheme rules, evidence, receiving banks, and law enforcement. |
| Privacy complaint | Handled with input from the Data Protection Office. |
The final response will explain the outcome, any redress, and escalation rights where applicable.

Privacy, Data Protection & Open Banking
10. Open banking
Open banking allows a customer to give a regulated third-party provider access to account information or payment initiation services. Aurora Bank will provide access only after the customer gives permission through the required secure process.
Important open banking points:
- Aurora Bank will never ask the customer to share online banking passwords with a third-party provider.
- The customer can withdraw open banking consent through Aurora online banking or the third-party provider.
- Revoking access does not delete data already received by the third-party provider.
- The third-party provider is responsible for its own use of data after it receives it.
- Payment initiation through open banking may still require strong customer authentication.
Customers should use only regulated providers and should check the provider name carefully before approving access.

10. Open banking
Open banking allows a customer to give a regulated third-party provider access to account information or payment initiation services. Aurora Bank will provide access only after the customer gives permission through the required secure process.
Important open banking points:
- Aurora Bank will never ask the customer to share online banking passwords with a third-party provider.
- The customer can withdraw open banking consent through Aurora online banking or the third-party provider.
- Revoking access does not delete data already received by the third-party provider.
- The third-party provider is responsible for its own use of data after it receives it.
- Payment initiation through open banking may still require strong customer authentication.
Customers should use only regulated providers and should check the provider name carefully before approving access.

Aurora Bank uses layered security controls to protect accounts. These controls may include encryption, device binding, login monitoring, fraud scoring, strong customer authentication, payment warnings, transaction limits, account locks, and manual review.

6. Account purpose and expected activity
We will ask why the customer wants the account and what types of transactions are expected. Examples include salary receipt, rent and bills, family support, savings, travel spending, student living expenses, pension income, or general day-to-day banking.
Customers must not use a personal account for business trading, client money, payment processing on behalf of others, unregistered charity activity, or money-service activity. Sole traders and freelancers may need a separate business account if business income and expenses are regular or material.

Cards, Debit Cards, Credit Cards, ATMs & Mobile Wallets
7. ATM cash withdrawals and deposits
Customers can use eligible cards at Aurora ATMs and participating network ATMs. ATM operators may charge their own fees or display conversion options. Aurora Bank does not control fees charged by non-Aurora ATM operators.
ATM services may include cash withdrawal, balance inquiry, PIN change, mini-statement, and cash deposit where available. Cash deposits at ATMs may be subject to counting, verification, counterfeit detection, and delayed availability.
Customers should check the ATM area for tampering, shield the PIN, take receipts, and contact Aurora Bank if the ATM does not dispense cash but the account is debited.

4. Account balances
The **ledger balance** is the balance after transactions already posted to the account. The **available balance** is the amount available for use after pending transactions, card authorizations, overdraft limits, account restrictions, and holds are considered.

5. Inactive accounts
An account may be marked inactive after 12 months without customer-initiated activity or meaningful customer contact. Activity can include a customer payment, card transaction, branch visit, secure message, login with confirmed identity, or signed instruction.
Automated interest, fees, or bank-initiated entries do not always count as customer activity.
Aurora Bank may reduce statements, block new cards, lower limits, or request updated customer information on inactive accounts.

Aurora Bank may change fees and variable rates after notice. Some changes can take effect immediately where required by law, security, payment-scheme rules, tax, or regulatory change. Customers may be able to repay a loan early in full or make overpayments. Early repayment can reduce total interest but may trigger an early-repayment charge if allowed by law and the credit agreement.
For partial overpayments, Aurora Bank may reduce the remaining term, reduce monthly payments, or hold the overpayment until recalculation, depending on product terms and customer instruction.

Aurora Bank may offer temporary support if a customer is experiencing financial difficulty. Support can include payment deferral, temporary reduced payments, interest-only periods, debt advice referral, breathing-space arrangements, or restructuring.
Support is not automatic and may affect credit records, total interest, product eligibility, or future borrowing. Customers should provide accurate information about income, expenses, assets, debts, and the cause of difficulty.

heading_path: 8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments

retrieved_chunks.content:
Current & Savings Accounts Terms
8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments
Direct debits are authorized by the customer to allow a payee to collect variable or fixed amounts. Standing orders are instructions created by the customer to pay a fixed amount on a schedule. Recurring card payments are card-authorized merchant arrangements and are not the same as direct debits.
Cancellation rules differ:
- A standing order can normally be cancelled in online banking before the processing cutoff.
- A direct debit can be cancelled with Aurora Bank, but the customer should also cancel the agreement with the merchant.
- A recurring card payment should be cancelled with the merchant. Aurora Bank can block future merchant attempts in some cases, but this may not cancel the underlying contract.
Payment execution and cancellation timings are described in [Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times](03_payments_transfers_and_cutoff_times.md).

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
8. Direct debits
A direct debit allows an organization to collect money from the customer’s account under a mandate. The customer should receive advance notice from the payee unless the scheme rules allow otherwise.
Aurora Bank can cancel a direct debit mandate on the account, but this does not cancel the underlying contract with the merchant. The merchant may still claim the amount by another method or treat the customer as overdue.
Where a direct debit is unauthorized or collected incorrectly, the customer may have refund rights under applicable payment-scheme and legal rules. Dispute processes are explained in [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md).

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
10. Direct debit refunds
If a direct debit was collected without a valid mandate, for the wrong amount, on the wrong date, or after cancellation, the customer should contact Aurora Bank. Aurora Bank may request mandate details and merchant communications.
Cancelling a direct debit with Aurora Bank stops future collections from that mandate where possible. It does not cancel the customer’s contract with the merchant.

retrieved_chunks.content:

11. Cancelling, recalling, or amending a payment
Cancellation rights depend on payment type.
| Payment type | Can the customer cancel? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Future-dated SEPA payment | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before execution. | Online cancellation may be available. |
| Standing order | Usually yes before the cutoff for the next due date. | Cancelling does not cancel contracts with merchants. |
| Direct debit | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before collection. | Customer should also notify the payee. |
| SEPA instant transfer | Usually no once authorized. | Recall can be attempted but is not guaranteed. |
| Standard SEPA transfer | Recall can be requested after execution. | Recipient bank and recipient consent may be required. |
| International wire | Amendment or recall can be requested. | Fees apply and recovery is not guaranteed. |
| Card purchase | Customer should first contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. | Chargeback may be possible under card scheme rules. |
Aurora Bank cannot guarantee recovery of funds sent to the wrong recipient if the payment was authorized by the customer. The bank may try to contact the receiving bank, but the recipient may need to consent to return funds unless legal rules allow reversal.

5. Overdraft fees and interest
Arranged overdraft interest is calculated daily on the used arranged overdraft balance and charged monthly. The illustrative arranged overdraft rate is 13.90% annual nominal variable.

8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments
Direct debits are authorized by the customer to allow a payee to collect variable or fixed amounts. Standing orders are instructions created by the customer to pay a fixed amount on a schedule. Recurring card payments are card-authorized merchant arrangements and are not the same as direct debits.
Cancellation rules differ:
- A standing order can normally be cancelled in online banking before the processing cutoff.
- A direct debit can be cancelled with Aurora Bank, but the customer should also cancel the agreement with the merchant.
- A recurring card payment should be cancelled with the merchant. Aurora Bank can block future merchant attempts in some cases, but this may not cancel the underlying contract.
Payment execution and cancellation timings are described in [Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times](03_payments_transfers_and_cutoff_times.md).

8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments
Direct debits are authorized by the customer to allow a payee to collect variable or fixed amounts. Standing orders are instructions created by the customer to pay a fixed amount on a schedule. Recurring card payments are card-authorized merchant arrangements and are not the same as direct debits.
Cancellation rules differ:
- A standing order can normally be cancelled in online banking before the processing cutoff.
- A direct debit can be cancelled with Aurora Bank, but the customer should also cancel the agreement with the merchant.

heading_path: 3. What Aurora Bank will never ask for

retrieved_chunks.content:
Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
1. Security principles
Aurora Bank uses layered security controls to protect accounts. These controls may include encryption, device binding, login monitoring, fraud scoring, strong customer authentication, payment warnings, transaction limits, account locks, and manual review.
Security controls may occasionally delay payments, block card use, restrict online access, or require additional verification. Aurora Bank will not compensate for inconvenience where a control was applied reasonably for safety or legal compliance.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
7. New payee and payment verification
When setting up a new payee, customers should verify the account number through a trusted channel. For invoices, the customer should confirm changes to bank details using a known phone number, not contact details on the changed invoice.
Aurora Bank may delay, hold, or reject first payments to new payees, high-risk merchants, crypto-asset platforms, or countries with elevated risk.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
6. Payment warnings
Aurora Bank may show warnings before high-risk payments. Customers should read warnings carefully. If a warning says the payment may be a scam, the customer should pause and verify independently.
A customer should not continue a payment because someone on the phone instructs them to do so. Scammers often coach victims to bypass warnings or mislead the bank.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
2. Strong customer authentication
Strong customer authentication uses at least two independent elements from the following categories:
- something the customer knows, such as password or PIN;
- something the customer has, such as registered device or hardware token;
- something the customer is, such as fingerprint or facial recognition.
Some low-risk transactions may be exempt, but Aurora Bank may still require authentication based on fraud risk, transaction amount, merchant type, new device, new payee, unusual behavior, or regulatory rules.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
10. Secure messages and document upload
Customers should send sensitive information only through approved secure channels. Documents uploaded to online banking should be clear, complete, and unaltered. Aurora Bank may reject documents that are cropped, blurry, password-protected, edited, or inconsistent.
Customers should not send identity documents, card numbers, passwords, or one-time passcodes through ordinary email unless specifically instructed through a secure process.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
11. Social media and public channels
Aurora Bank may provide general support through social media but will not conduct full account servicing through public comments. Customers should not post account numbers, card numbers, personal documents, transaction details, or complaint evidence publicly.

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
12. Staff conduct
Customers and staff are expected to treat each other respectfully. Aurora Bank may restrict communication channels if a customer uses abusive, threatening, discriminatory, or persistently unreasonable behavior. We will still try to preserve access to essential banking services where safe and lawful.

10. Open banking
Open banking allows a customer to give a regulated third-party provider access to account information or payment initiation services. Aurora Bank will provide access only after the customer gives permission through the required secure process.
Important open banking points:
- Aurora Bank will never ask the customer to share online banking passwords with a third-party provider.
- The customer can withdraw open banking consent through Aurora online banking or the third-party provider.
- Revoking access does not delete data already received by the third-party provider.
- The third-party provider is responsible for its own use of data after it receives it.
- Payment initiation through open banking may still require strong customer authentication.
Customers should use only regulated providers and should check the provider name carefully before approving access.

11. Domestic abuse and financial abuse
Aurora Bank recognizes that financial abuse can include controlling access to money, coercing loans, intercepting cards, monitoring statements, forcing transfers, or misusing joint accounts.
Customers can request confidential support. Aurora Bank can discuss safe contact methods, correspondence suppression, card replacement, account separation options, payment controls, and referral to specialist organizations. Joint account changes may require legal or operational safeguards.

2. Types of disputes
| Dispute type | Examples | Typical first step |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Card stolen, card details used online, wallet token compromised | Freeze card and report fraud. |
| Merchant card dispute | Goods not received, defective goods, duplicate charge, cancelled subscription | Contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. |
| ATM dispute | Cash not dispensed, partial dispense, retained card | Report ATM location, date, amount. |
| Direct debit dispute | Wrong amount, no mandate, collected after cancellation | Request direct debit investigation or refund. |
| Bank transfer recall | Payment sent to wrong IBAN or scam recipient | Request recall immediately; recovery not guaranteed. |
| Incoming payment missing | Expected payment not credited | Ask sender for payment proof and trace reference. |
| Fee dispute | Bank fee appears incorrect | Contact customer service with transaction details. |
Different schemes and laws have different deadlines, evidence standards, and refund rules.

13. Payment disputes and unauthorized payments
Customers should report unauthorized or incorrect payments as soon as they notice them. Fast reporting improves the chance of stopping further loss and recovering funds.
Unauthorized electronic payments, scam payments, direct debit errors, card disputes, and merchant chargebacks are handled under [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md). Security steps are described in [Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities](09_security_online_banking_and_customer_responsibilities.md).

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
9. Card payment authorization and settlement
A card transaction usually has two stages:
1. **Authorization**: the merchant requests approval and the available balance is reduced.
2. **Settlement**: the merchant presents the final transaction and it posts to the account.
The settlement amount can differ from the authorization amount because of tips, currency conversion, fuel pre-authorizations, hotel deposits, delayed transit fares, or partial shipments. Card rules are described in [Cards, Debit Cards, Credit Cards, ATMs & Mobile Wallets](04_cards_debit_credit_atm_mobile_wallets.md).

14. Merchant refunds

6. Time limits
Customers should raise disputes promptly. Card-scheme time limits can be short and may run from transaction date, expected delivery date, cancellation date, or merchant promise date.
Indicative timeframes:
| Claim type | Customer should report by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Immediately, and no later than 13 months where legal rules permit | Faster reporting can reduce loss. |
| Goods or services not received | After expected delivery date, usually within 120 days of expected receipt | Scheme rules vary. |
| Refund not processed | After merchant’s refund timeframe, usually within 120 days of refund promise | Evidence needed. |
| ATM cash not dispensed | Within 30 days if possible | ATM balancing may be time-sensitive. |
| Incorrect direct debit | As soon as noticed | Scheme and legal refund rights may apply. |
| Payment sent to wrong account | Immediately | Recovery becomes harder once funds move. |
The exact deadline depends on scheme and legal rules. Aurora Bank may be unable to pursue a claim filed too late.

11. Cancelling, recalling, or amending a payment
Cancellation rights depend on payment type.
| Payment type | Can the customer cancel? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Future-dated SEPA payment | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before execution. | Online cancellation may be available. |
| Standing order | Usually yes before the cutoff for the next due date. | Cancelling does not cancel contracts with merchants. |
| Direct debit | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before collection. | Customer should also notify the payee. |
| SEPA instant transfer | Usually no once authorized. | Recall can be attempted but is not guaranteed. |
| Standard SEPA transfer | Recall can be requested after execution. | Recipient bank and recipient consent may be required. |
| International wire | Amendment or recall can be requested. | Fees apply and recovery is not guaranteed. |
| Card purchase | Customer should first contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. | Chargeback may be possible under card scheme rules. |
Aurora Bank cannot guarantee recovery of funds sent to the wrong recipient if the payment was authorized by the customer. The bank may try to contact the receiving bank, but the recipient may need to consent to return funds unless legal rules allow reversal.

6. Lost, stolen, damaged, or retained card
If a card is lost, stolen, retained by an ATM, or used without permission, the customer should immediately freeze the card in the app and contact Aurora Bank. Emergency contact options are listed in [Glossary, Contact Channels & Service Levels](12_glossary_contact_and_service_level.md).
Aurora Bank may cancel the card and issue a replacement. A replacement-card fee may apply unless the loss was caused by bank error, fraud, expiry, or another fee-waiver circumstance.
Customers should review recent transactions and report unauthorized card transactions promptly under [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md).

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
6. Time limits
Customers should raise disputes promptly. Card-scheme time limits can be short and may run from transaction date, expected delivery date, cancellation date, or merchant promise date.
Indicative timeframes:
| Claim type | Customer should report by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Immediately, and no later than 13 months where legal rules permit | Faster reporting can reduce loss. |
| Goods or services not received | After expected delivery date, usually within 120 days of expected receipt | Scheme rules vary. |
| Refund not processed | After merchant’s refund timeframe, usually within 120 days of refund promise | Evidence needed. |
| ATM cash not dispensed | Within 30 days if possible | ATM balancing may be time-sensitive. |
| Incorrect direct debit | As soon as noticed | Scheme and legal refund rights may apply. |
| Payment sent to wrong account | Immediately | Recovery becomes harder once funds move. |
The exact deadline depends on scheme and legal rules. Aurora Bank may be unable to pursue a claim filed too late.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
8. Direct debits
A direct debit allows an organization to collect money from the customer’s account under a mandate. The customer should receive advance notice from the payee unless the scheme rules allow otherwise.
Aurora Bank can cancel a direct debit mandate on the account, but this does not cancel the underlying contract with the merchant. The merchant may still claim the amount by another method or treat the customer as overdue.
Where a direct debit is unauthorized or collected incorrectly, the customer may have refund rights under applicable payment-scheme and legal rules. Dispute processes are explained in [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md).

8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments
Direct debits are authorized by the customer to allow a payee to collect variable or fixed amounts. Standing orders are instructions created by the customer to pay a fixed amount on a schedule. Recurring card payments are card-authorized merchant arrangements and are not the same as direct debits.
Cancellation rules differ:
- A standing order can normally be cancelled in online banking before the processing cutoff.
- A direct debit can be cancelled with Aurora Bank, but the customer should also cancel the agreement with the merchant.
- A recurring card payment should be cancelled with the merchant. Aurora Bank can block future merchant attempts in some cases, but this may not cancel the underlying contract.
Payment execution and cancellation timings are described in [Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times](03_payments_transfers_and_cutoff_times.md).

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
6. Time limits
Customers should raise disputes promptly. Card-scheme time limits can be short and may run from transaction date, expected delivery date, cancellation date, or merchant promise date.
Indicative timeframes:
| Claim type | Customer should report by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Immediately, and no later than 13 months where legal rules permit | Faster reporting can reduce loss. |
| Goods or services not received | After expected delivery date, usually within 120 days of expected receipt | Scheme rules vary. |
| Refund not processed | After merchant’s refund timeframe, usually within 120 days of refund promise | Evidence needed. |
| ATM cash not dispensed | Within 30 days if possible | ATM balancing may be time-sensitive. |
| Incorrect direct debit | As soon as noticed | Scheme and legal refund rights may apply. |
| Payment sent to wrong account | Immediately | Recovery becomes harder once funds move. |
The exact deadline depends on scheme and legal rules. Aurora Bank may be unable to pursue a claim filed too late.

Current & Savings Accounts Terms
8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments
Direct debits are authorized by the customer to allow a payee to collect variable or fixed amounts. Standing orders are instructions created by the customer to pay a fixed amount on a schedule. Recurring card payments are card-authorized merchant arrangements and are not the same as direct debits.
Cancellation rules differ:
- A standing order can normally be cancelled in online banking before the processing cutoff.
- A direct debit can be cancelled with Aurora Bank, but the customer should also cancel the agreement with the merchant.
- A recurring card payment should be cancelled with the merchant. Aurora Bank can block future merchant attempts in some cases, but this may not cancel the underlying contract.
Payment execution and cancellation timings are described in [Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times](03_payments_transfers_and_cutoff_times.md).

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
8. Direct debits
A direct debit allows an organization to collect money from the customer’s account under a mandate. The customer should receive advance notice from the payee unless the scheme rules allow otherwise.
Aurora Bank can cancel a direct debit mandate on the account, but this does not cancel the underlying contract with the merchant. The merchant may still claim the amount by another method or treat the customer as overdue.
Where a direct debit is unauthorized or collected incorrectly, the customer may have refund rights under applicable payment-scheme and legal rules. Dispute processes are explained in [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md).

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
10. Direct debit refunds
If a direct debit was collected without a valid mandate, for the wrong amount, on the wrong date, or after cancellation, the customer should contact Aurora Bank. Aurora Bank may request mandate details and merchant communications.
Cancelling a direct debit with Aurora Bank stops future collections from that mandate where possible. It does not cancel the customer’s contract with the merchant.

10. Open banking
Open banking allows a customer to give a regulated third-party provider access to account information or payment initiation services. Aurora Bank will provide access only after the customer gives permission through the required secure process.
Important open banking points:
- Aurora Bank will never ask the customer to share online banking passwords with a third-party provider.
- The customer can withdraw open banking consent through Aurora online banking or the third-party provider.
- Revoking access does not delete data already received by the third-party provider.
- The third-party provider is responsible for its own use of data after it receives it.
- Payment initiation through open banking may still require strong customer authentication.
Customers should use only regulated providers and should check the provider name carefully before approving access.

Youth accounts, Basic Payment Accounts, savings accounts, and Fixed Term Deposits do not offer arranged overdrafts.

retrieved_chunks.content:
Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
11. Cancelling, recalling, or amending a payment
Cancellation rights depend on payment type.
| Payment type | Can the customer cancel? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Future-dated SEPA payment | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before execution. | Online cancellation may be available. |
| Standing order | Usually yes before the cutoff for the next due date. | Cancelling does not cancel contracts with merchants. |
| Direct debit | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before collection. | Customer should also notify the payee. |
| SEPA instant transfer | Usually no once authorized. | Recall can be attempted but is not guaranteed. |
| Standard SEPA transfer | Recall can be requested after execution. | Recipient bank and recipient consent may be required. |
| International wire | Amendment or recall can be requested. | Fees apply and recovery is not guaranteed. |
| Card purchase | Customer should first contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. | Chargeback may be possible under card scheme rules. |
Aurora Bank cannot guarantee recovery of funds sent to the wrong recipient if the payment was authorized by the customer. The bank may try to contact the receiving bank, but the recipient may need to consent to return funds unless legal rules allow reversal.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
13. Payment disputes and unauthorized payments
Customers should report unauthorized or incorrect payments as soon as they notice them. Fast reporting improves the chance of stopping further loss and recovering funds.
Unauthorized electronic payments, scam payments, direct debit errors, card disputes, and merchant chargebacks are handled under [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md). Security steps are described in [Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities](09_security_online_banking_and_customer_responsibilities.md).

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
6. Time limits
Customers should raise disputes promptly. Card-scheme time limits can be short and may run from transaction date, expected delivery date, cancellation date, or merchant promise date.
Indicative timeframes:
| Claim type | Customer should report by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Immediately, and no later than 13 months where legal rules permit | Faster reporting can reduce loss. |
| Goods or services not received | After expected delivery date, usually within 120 days of expected receipt | Scheme rules vary. |
| Refund not processed | After merchant’s refund timeframe, usually within 120 days of refund promise | Evidence needed. |
| ATM cash not dispensed | Within 30 days if possible | ATM balancing may be time-sensitive. |
| Incorrect direct debit | As soon as noticed | Scheme and legal refund rights may apply. |
| Payment sent to wrong account | Immediately | Recovery becomes harder once funds move. |
The exact deadline depends on scheme and legal rules. Aurora Bank may be unable to pursue a claim filed too late.

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
10. Direct debit refunds
If a direct debit was collected without a valid mandate, for the wrong amount, on the wrong date, or after cancellation, the customer should contact Aurora Bank. Aurora Bank may request mandate details and merchant communications.
Cancelling a direct debit with Aurora Bank stops future collections from that mandate where possible. It does not cancel the customer’s contract with the merchant.

5. Escalation and external review

The final response will include relevant escalation information where required.
Customers usually must complain to Aurora Bank before using an external dispute resolution body.

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
This document explains how Aurora Bank handles complaints and supports customers who need additional help. Contact routes and service levels are listed in [Glossary, Contact Channels & Service Levels](12_glossary_contact_and_service_level.md).

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
3. Complaint acknowledgement and response times
Aurora Bank will acknowledge complaints promptly. Where possible, we resolve simple complaints within three business days. More complex complaints may take longer.
Indicative response standards:
| Complaint type | Expected handling |
|---|---|
| Simple service issue | Aim to resolve within 3 business days. |
| Standard complaint | Written final response normally within 15 business days for payment-service complaints, or within 30 calendar days for other complaints where local rules allow. |
| Complex complaint | If more time is needed, Aurora Bank will explain the delay and provide a final response within the maximum period required by law. |
| Fraud, chargeback, or scam complaint | Investigation timelines depend on scheme rules, evidence, receiving banks, and law enforcement. |
| Privacy complaint | Handled with input from the Data Protection Office. |
The final response will explain the outcome, any redress, and escalation rights where applicable.

Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment
13. Payment holidays and hardship support
Aurora Bank may offer temporary support if a customer is experiencing financial difficulty. Support can include payment deferral, temporary reduced payments, interest-only periods, debt advice referral, breathing-space arrangements, or restructuring.
Support is not automatic and may affect credit records, total interest, product eligibility, or future borrowing. Customers should provide accurate information about income, expenses, assets, debts, and the cause of difficulty.
Vulnerable-customer support is described in [Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility](10_complaints_vulnerable_customers_and_accessibility.md).

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
12. Staff conduct
Customers and staff are expected to treat each other respectfully. Aurora Bank may restrict communication channels if a customer uses abusive, threatening, discriminatory, or persistently unreasonable behavior. We will still try to preserve access to essential banking services where safe and lawful.

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
11. Domestic abuse and financial abuse
Aurora Bank recognizes that financial abuse can include controlling access to money, coercing loans, intercepting cards, monitoring statements, forcing transfers, or misusing joint accounts.
Customers can request confidential support. Aurora Bank can discuss safe contact methods, correspondence suppression, card replacement, account separation options, payment controls, and referral to specialist organizations. Joint account changes may require legal or operational safeguards.

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
8. Third-party authority and support persons
A customer can ask Aurora Bank to communicate with a support person. The level of access depends on authority provided:
| Authority type | What it usually allows |
|---|---|
| Trusted contact | Aurora Bank may contact the person if concerned about customer welfare or financial harm; no transaction authority. |
| One-time verbal authority | Discussion of a specific matter during a call or appointment. |
| Third-party mandate | Ongoing account discussion or limited account operation, depending on mandate. |
| Power of attorney | Legal authority according to the document and local law. |
| Guardian or court-appointed representative | Authority defined by court or law. |
Power of attorney and estates processes are described in [Account Closure, Inactivity, Estates & Power of Attorney](11_account_closure_inactivity_estates_and_power_of_attorney.md).

1. Card types
Aurora Bank may issue the following card types:
| Card type | Linked to | Main purpose | Key restrictions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Debit card | Current account | Spending the customer’s own available funds | No borrowing unless an overdraft is available. |

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
6. Time limits
Customers should raise disputes promptly. Card-scheme time limits can be short and may run from transaction date, expected delivery date, cancellation date, or merchant promise date.
Indicative timeframes:
| Claim type | Customer should report by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Immediately, and no later than 13 months where legal rules permit | Faster reporting can reduce loss. |
| Goods or services not received | After expected delivery date, usually within 120 days of expected receipt | Scheme rules vary. |
| Refund not processed | After merchant’s refund timeframe, usually within 120 days of refund promise | Evidence needed. |
| ATM cash not dispensed | Within 30 days if possible | ATM balancing may be time-sensitive. |
| Incorrect direct debit | As soon as noticed | Scheme and legal refund rights may apply. |
| Payment sent to wrong account | Immediately | Recovery becomes harder once funds move. |
The exact deadline depends on scheme and legal rules. Aurora Bank may be unable to pursue a claim filed too late.

We will ask why the customer wants the account and what types of transactions are expected. Examples include salary receipt, rent and bills, family support, savings, travel spending, student living expenses, pension income, or general day-to-day banking.
Customers must not use a personal account for business trading, client money, payment processing on behalf of others, unregistered charity activity, or money-service activity. Sole traders and freelancers may need a separate business account if business income and expenses are regular or material.

Privacy, Data Protection & Open Banking
10. Open banking
Open banking allows a customer to give a regulated third-party provider access to account information or payment initiation services. Aurora Bank will provide access only after the customer gives permission through the required secure process.
Important open banking points:
- Aurora Bank will never ask the customer to share online banking passwords with a third-party provider.
- The customer can withdraw open banking consent through Aurora online banking or the third-party provider.
- Revoking access does not delete data already received by the third-party provider.
- The third-party provider is responsible for its own use of data after it receives it.
- Payment initiation through open banking may still require strong customer authentication.
Customers should use only regulated providers and should check the provider name carefully before approving access.

3. Complaint acknowledgement and response times
Aurora Bank will acknowledge complaints promptly. Where possible, we resolve simple complaints within three business days. More complex complaints may take longer.
Indicative response standards:
| Complaint type | Expected handling |
|---|---|
| Simple service issue | Aim to resolve within 3 business days. |
| Standard complaint | Written final response normally within 15 business days for payment-service complaints, or within 30 calendar days for other complaints where local rules allow. |
| Complex complaint | If more time is needed, Aurora Bank will explain the delay and provide a final response within the maximum period required by law. |
| Fraud, chargeback, or scam complaint | Investigation timelines depend on scheme rules, evidence, receiving banks, and law enforcement. |
| Privacy complaint | Handled with input from the Data Protection Office. |
The final response will explain the outcome, any redress, and escalation rights where applicable.

13. Customer cooperation

| Dispute type | Examples | Typical first step |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Card stolen, card details used online, wallet token compromised | Freeze card and report fraud. |
| Merchant card dispute | Goods not received, defective goods, duplicate charge, cancelled subscription | Contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. |

| Incoming payment missing | Expected payment not credited | Ask sender for payment proof and trace reference. |

6. Lost, stolen, damaged, or retained card
If a card is lost, stolen, retained by an ATM, or used without permission, the customer should immediately freeze the card in the app and contact Aurora Bank. Emergency contact options are listed in [Glossary, Contact Channels & Service Levels](12_glossary_contact_and_service_level.md).
Aurora Bank may cancel the card and issue a replacement. A replacement-card fee may apply unless the loss was caused by bank error, fraud, expiry, or another fee-waiver circumstance.

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
6. Time limits
Customers should raise disputes promptly. Card-scheme time limits can be short and may run from transaction date, expected delivery date, cancellation date, or merchant promise date.
Indicative timeframes:
| Claim type | Customer should report by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Immediately, and no later than 13 months where legal rules permit | Faster reporting can reduce loss. |
| Goods or services not received | After expected delivery date, usually within 120 days of expected receipt | Scheme rules vary. |
| Refund not processed | After merchant’s refund timeframe, usually within 120 days of refund promise | Evidence needed. |
| ATM cash not dispensed | Within 30 days if possible | ATM balancing may be time-sensitive. |
| Incorrect direct debit | As soon as noticed | Scheme and legal refund rights may apply. |
| Payment sent to wrong account | Immediately | Recovery becomes harder once funds move. |
The exact deadline depends on scheme and legal rules. Aurora Bank may be unable to pursue a claim filed too late.

8. Scams and authorized push payment fraud
A scam payment occurs when a customer is tricked into authorizing a payment. Examples include impersonation scams, investment scams, romance scams, invoice redirection, purchase scams, and safe-account scams.
Aurora Bank will review scam reports and may attempt recovery from the receiving bank. Refund outcomes depend on law, scheme rules, customer conduct, warning effectiveness, and whether funds remain recoverable. Customers should report immediately and preserve evidence such as messages, phone numbers, websites, invoices, and payment instructions.
If a customer is currently speaking to a suspected scammer, they should end the call or chat and contact Aurora Bank using a known channel, not a number provided by the caller.

retrieved_chunks.content:
Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
11. Cancelling, recalling, or amending a payment
Cancellation rights depend on payment type.
| Payment type | Can the customer cancel? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Future-dated SEPA payment | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before execution. | Online cancellation may be available. |
| Standing order | Usually yes before the cutoff for the next due date. | Cancelling does not cancel contracts with merchants. |
| Direct debit | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before collection. | Customer should also notify the payee. |
| SEPA instant transfer | Usually no once authorized. | Recall can be attempted but is not guaranteed. |
| Standard SEPA transfer | Recall can be requested after execution. | Recipient bank and recipient consent may be required. |
| International wire | Amendment or recall can be requested. | Fees apply and recovery is not guaranteed. |
| Card purchase | Customer should first contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. | Chargeback may be possible under card scheme rules. |
Aurora Bank cannot guarantee recovery of funds sent to the wrong recipient if the payment was authorized by the customer. The bank may try to contact the receiving bank, but the recipient may need to consent to return funds unless legal rules allow reversal.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
13. Payment disputes and unauthorized payments
Customers should report unauthorized or incorrect payments as soon as they notice them. Fast reporting improves the chance of stopping further loss and recovering funds.
Unauthorized electronic payments, scam payments, direct debit errors, card disputes, and merchant chargebacks are handled under [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md). Security steps are described in [Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities](09_security_online_banking_and_customer_responsibilities.md).

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
6. Time limits
Customers should raise disputes promptly. Card-scheme time limits can be short and may run from transaction date, expected delivery date, cancellation date, or merchant promise date.
Indicative timeframes:
| Claim type | Customer should report by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Immediately, and no later than 13 months where legal rules permit | Faster reporting can reduce loss. |
| Goods or services not received | After expected delivery date, usually within 120 days of expected receipt | Scheme rules vary. |
| Refund not processed | After merchant’s refund timeframe, usually within 120 days of refund promise | Evidence needed. |
| ATM cash not dispensed | Within 30 days if possible | ATM balancing may be time-sensitive. |
| Incorrect direct debit | As soon as noticed | Scheme and legal refund rights may apply. |
| Payment sent to wrong account | Immediately | Recovery becomes harder once funds move. |
The exact deadline depends on scheme and legal rules. Aurora Bank may be unable to pursue a claim filed too late.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
3. Cutoff times
Cutoff times are shown in Central European Time unless otherwise stated. They can change during public holidays, system maintenance, or payment-scheme disruption.
| Payment type | Standard cutoff | Execution expectation |
|---|---:|---|
| SEPA Credit Transfer submitted in online banking | 15:30 on a business day | Sent same business day; usually credited by beneficiary bank by next business day. |
| SEPA Credit Transfer submitted in branch | 14:00 on a business day | Sent same business day if accepted before cutoff. |
| SEPA Instant Credit Transfer | 24/7 where available | Usually within seconds; may fall back or be declined if unavailable. |
| Internal transfer between own Aurora accounts | 24/7 | Usually immediate. |
| Internal transfer to another Aurora customer | 22:00 daily | Usually same day after security checks. |
| International wire in EUR | 13:00 on a business day | Usually 1-2 business days, depending on route. |
| International wire in non-EUR currency | 11:30 on a business day | Usually 2-5 business days, depending on currency and intermediaries. |
| Standing order creation or amendment | 18:00 the business day before due date | Changes after cutoff may apply to the next cycle only. |
| Direct debit cancellation | 18:00 the business day before collection date | Later cancellation may not stop the payment. |
Cutoff times are not promises that the beneficiary will receive funds at a specific hour. Intermediary banks, receiving banks, screening, incorrect details, and payment-system availability may affect timing.

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
3. Complaint acknowledgement and response times
Aurora Bank will acknowledge complaints promptly. Where possible, we resolve simple complaints within three business days. More complex complaints may take longer.
Indicative response standards:
| Complaint type | Expected handling |
|---|---|
| Simple service issue | Aim to resolve within 3 business days. |
| Standard complaint | Written final response normally within 15 business days for payment-service complaints, or within 30 calendar days for other complaints where local rules allow. |
| Complex complaint | If more time is needed, Aurora Bank will explain the delay and provide a final response within the maximum period required by law. |
| Fraud, chargeback, or scam complaint | Investigation timelines depend on scheme rules, evidence, receiving banks, and law enforcement. |
| Privacy complaint | Handled with input from the Data Protection Office. |
The final response will explain the outcome, any redress, and escalation rights where applicable.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
8. Direct debits
A direct debit allows an organization to collect money from the customer’s account under a mandate. The customer should receive advance notice from the payee unless the scheme rules allow otherwise.
Aurora Bank can cancel a direct debit mandate on the account, but this does not cancel the underlying contract with the merchant. The merchant may still claim the amount by another method or treat the customer as overdue.
Where a direct debit is unauthorized or collected incorrectly, the customer may have refund rights under applicable payment-scheme and legal rules. Dispute processes are explained in [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md).

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
9. Card payment authorization and settlement
A card transaction usually has two stages:
1. **Authorization**: the merchant requests approval and the available balance is reduced.
2. **Settlement**: the merchant presents the final transaction and it posts to the account.
The settlement amount can differ from the authorization amount because of tips, currency conversion, fuel pre-authorizations, hotel deposits, delayed transit fares, or partial shipments. Card rules are described in [Cards, Debit Cards, Credit Cards, ATMs & Mobile Wallets](04_cards_debit_credit_atm_mobile_wallets.md).

10. Recurring card payments and subscriptions
A recurring card payment is an agreement between the customer and merchant to charge a card repeatedly. Examples include streaming services, gym memberships, software subscriptions, and app purchases.
To stop a recurring card payment, the customer should cancel with the merchant. Aurora Bank can help block future attempts from a merchant in some cases, but this may not end the customer’s contract. If the merchant keeps charging after cancellation, the customer may raise a dispute with evidence of cancellation.

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
2. Types of disputes
| Dispute type | Examples | Typical first step |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Card stolen, card details used online, wallet token compromised | Freeze card and report fraud. |
| Merchant card dispute | Goods not received, defective goods, duplicate charge, cancelled subscription | Contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. |
| ATM dispute | Cash not dispensed, partial dispense, retained card | Report ATM location, date, amount. |
| Direct debit dispute | Wrong amount, no mandate, collected after cancellation | Request direct debit investigation or refund. |
| Bank transfer recall | Payment sent to wrong IBAN or scam recipient | Request recall immediately; recovery not guaranteed. |
| Incoming payment missing | Expected payment not credited | Ask sender for payment proof and trace reference. |
| Fee dispute | Bank fee appears incorrect | Contact customer service with transaction details. |
Different schemes and laws have different deadlines, evidence standards, and refund rules.

2. Types of disputes
| Dispute type | Examples | Typical first step |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Card stolen, card details used online, wallet token compromised | Freeze card and report fraud. |
| Merchant card dispute | Goods not received, defective goods, duplicate charge, cancelled subscription | Contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. |
| ATM dispute | Cash not dispensed, partial dispense, retained card | Report ATM location, date, amount. |
| Direct debit dispute | Wrong amount, no mandate, collected after cancellation | Request direct debit investigation or refund. |
| Bank transfer recall | Payment sent to wrong IBAN or scam recipient | Request recall immediately; recovery not guaranteed. |
| Incoming payment missing | Expected payment not credited | Ask sender for payment proof and trace reference. |

3. Cutoff times
Cutoff times are shown in Central European Time unless otherwise stated. They can change during public holidays, system maintenance, or payment-scheme disruption.
| Payment type | Standard cutoff | Execution expectation |
|---|---:|---|
| SEPA Credit Transfer submitted in online banking | 15:30 on a business day | Sent same business day; usually credited by beneficiary bank by next business day. |
| SEPA Credit Transfer submitted in branch | 14:00 on a business day | Sent same business day if accepted before cutoff. |
| SEPA Instant Credit Transfer | 24/7 where available | Usually within seconds; may fall back or be declined if unavailable. |
| Internal transfer between own Aurora accounts | 24/7 | Usually immediate. |
| Internal transfer to another Aurora customer | 22:00 daily | Usually same day after security checks. |
| International wire in EUR | 13:00 on a business day | Usually 1-2 business days, depending on route. |
| International wire in non-EUR currency | 11:30 on a business day | Usually 2-5 business days, depending on currency and intermediaries. |
| Standing order creation or amendment | 18:00 the business day before due date | Changes after cutoff may apply to the next cycle only. |
| Direct debit cancellation | 18:00 the business day before collection date | Later cancellation may not stop the payment. |
Cutoff times are not promises that the beneficiary will receive funds at a specific hour. Intermediary banks, receiving banks, screening, incorrect details, and payment-system availability may affect timing.

chunk.content:

11. Cancelling, recalling, or amending a payment
Cancellation rights depend on payment type.
| Payment type | Can the customer cancel? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Future-dated SEPA payment | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before execution. | Online cancellation may be available. |
| Standing order | Usually yes before the cutoff for the next due date. | Cancelling does not cancel contracts with merchants. |
| Direct debit | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before collection. | Customer should also notify the payee. |
| SEPA instant transfer | Usually no once authorized. | Recall can be attempted but is not guaranteed. |
| Standard SEPA transfer | Recall can be requested after execution. | Recipient bank and recipient consent may be required. |
| International wire | Amendment or recall can be requested. | Fees apply and recovery is not guaranteed. |
| Card purchase | Customer should first contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. | Chargeback may be possible under card scheme rules. |
Aurora Bank cannot guarantee recovery of funds sent to the wrong recipient if the payment was authorized by the customer. The bank may try to contact the receiving bank, but the recipient may need to consent to return funds unless legal rules allow reversal.

8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments

2. Types of disputes
| Dispute type | Examples | Typical first step |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Card stolen, card details used online, wallet token compromised | Freeze card and report fraud. |
| Merchant card dispute | Goods not received, defective goods, duplicate charge, cancelled subscription | Contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. |
| ATM dispute | Cash not dispensed, partial dispense, retained card | Report ATM location, date, amount. |
| Direct debit dispute | Wrong amount, no mandate, collected after cancellation | Request direct debit investigation or refund. |
| Bank transfer recall | Payment sent to wrong IBAN or scam recipient | Request recall immediately; recovery not guaranteed. |
| Incoming payment missing | Expected payment not credited | Ask sender for payment proof and trace reference. |
| Fee dispute | Bank fee appears incorrect | Contact customer service with transaction details. |
Different schemes and laws have different deadlines, evidence standards, and refund rules.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
13. Payment disputes and unauthorized payments
Customers should report unauthorized or incorrect payments as soon as they notice them. Fast reporting improves the chance of stopping further loss and recovering funds.
Unauthorized electronic payments, scam payments, direct debit errors, card disputes, and merchant chargebacks are handled under [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md). Aurora Bank may show warnings before high-risk payments. Customers should read warnings carefully. If a warning says the payment may be a scam, the customer should pause and verify independently.
A customer should not continue a payment because someone on the phone instructs them to do so. Scammers often coach victims to bypass warnings or mislead the bank.

2. Types of disputes
| Dispute type | Examples | Typical first step |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Card stolen, card details used online, wallet token compromised | Freeze card and report fraud. |
| Merchant card dispute | Goods not received, defective goods, duplicate charge, cancelled subscription | Contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. |
| ATM dispute | Cash not dispensed, partial dispense, retained card | Report ATM location, date, amount. |
| Direct debit dispute | Wrong amount, no mandate, collected after cancellation | Request direct debit investigation or refund. |
| Bank transfer recall | Payment sent to wrong IBAN or scam recipient | Request recall immediately; recovery not guaranteed. |
| Incoming payment missing | Expected payment not credited | Ask sender for payment proof and trace reference. |
| Fee dispute | Bank fee appears incorrect | Contact customer service with transaction details. |
Different schemes and laws have different deadlines, evidence standards, and refund rules.

3. Savings account core services
3.3 Fixed Term Deposit
A Fixed Term Deposit is opened for a fixed period and pays a fixed interest rate. Additional deposits and partial withdrawals are not normally allowed after the funding window closes. Early closure is not normally available unless required by law or approved due to hardship.

Current & Savings Accounts Terms
6. Overdraft basics
An arranged overdraft is a credit facility attached to a current account. It allows the balance to go below zero up to an approved limit. Arranged overdrafts are subject to credit assessment and are not guaranteed. Details are in [Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment](05_loans_overdrafts_and_credit_assessment.md).
An unarranged overdraft occurs when the account goes below zero without approval or exceeds an arranged limit. Aurora Bank may refuse payments that would create or increase an unarranged overdraft. Fees and interest may apply as described in [Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange](06_fees_interest_and_exchange_rates.md).
Youth accounts, Basic Payment Accounts, savings accounts, and Fixed Term Deposits do not offer arranged overdrafts.

Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange
7. Savings interest
Savings interest can be fixed or variable. Variable rates may change after notice. Fixed Term Deposit rates are fixed for the term once the deposit is opened and funded.
Illustrative annual gross rates:
| Product | Interest rate type | Indicative annual gross rate |
|---|---|---:|
| Instant Saver | Variable | 1.20% |
| 32-Day Notice Saver | Variable | 1.85% |
| 90-Day Notice Saver | Variable | 2.10% |
| 12-Month Fixed Term Deposit | Fixed | 2.40% |
Interest is normally calculated daily on cleared balance and paid monthly or annually depending on product terms. Tax may be withheld or reported depending on the customer’s tax status and local law.

Glossary, Contact Channels & Service Levels
3. Definitions
Overdraft
A credit facility that allows a current account balance to go below zero, subject to approval and terms.

Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment
9. Arranged overdrafts
An arranged overdraft is intended as a short-term borrowing facility. It should not be used for long-term borrowing or regular living costs. Aurora Bank may review, reduce, suspend, or cancel an overdraft after notice or immediately where required for risk, fraud, legal, or account-conduct reasons.
Important overdraft rules:
- Interest is charged only on the used arranged overdraft balance.
- The overdraft is repayable on demand.
- Exceeding the limit may lead to declined payments and fees.
- An overdraft limit is not a promise that every payment will be honored.
- Savings accounts and youth accounts do not have overdrafts.

Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment
8. Interest rates and representative examples
Loan interest rates can be fixed or variable depending on product terms. The final rate may depend on credit assessment, loan amount, term, product type, collateral, account relationship, and market conditions.
A representative example is only an illustration. It does not guarantee that a customer will receive that rate. Interest, annual percentage rate, arrangement fees, early-repayment charges, and late-payment charges are described in the customer’s credit agreement and [Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange](06_fees_interest_and_exchange_rates.md).

8. Direct debits, standing orders, and recurring payments
Direct debits are authorized by the customer to allow a payee to collect variable or fixed amounts. Standing orders are instructions created by the customer to pay a fixed amount on a schedule. Recurring card payments are card-authorized merchant arrangements and are not the same as direct debits.
Cancellation rules differ:
- A standing order can normally be cancelled in online banking before the processing cutoff.
- A direct debit can be cancelled with Aurora Bank, but the customer should also cancel the agreement with the merchant.
- A recurring card payment should be cancelled with the merchant. Aurora Bank can block future merchant attempts in some cases, but this may not cancel the underlying contract.
Payment execution and cancellation timings are described in [Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times](03_payments_transfers_and_cutoff_times.md).

Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange
5. Overdraft fees and interest
Arranged overdraft interest is calculated daily on the used arranged overdraft balance and charged monthly. The illustrative arranged overdraft rate is 13.90% annual nominal variable.
Aurora Bank does not charge a separate daily unarranged overdraft fee in this mock fee schedule. However, payments that exceed the available balance may be rejected and failed-payment fees may apply where permitted. If an unarranged negative balance occurs, debit interest may be charged and the customer must repay it immediately.
The bank may reduce or waive fees where financial difficulty is confirmed. Hardship support is described in [Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment](05_loans_overdrafts_and_credit_assessment.md).

Unarranged overdraft
A negative balance that occurs without an approved overdraft or above the arranged overdraft limit.

6. Lost, stolen, damaged, or retained card
If a card is lost, stolen, retained by an ATM, or used without permission, the customer should immediately freeze the card in the app and contact Aurora Bank. Emergency contact options are listed in [Glossary, Contact Channels & Service Levels](12_glossary_contact_and_service_level.md).
Aurora Bank may cancel the card and issue a replacement. A replacement-card fee may apply unless the loss was caused by bank error, fraud, expiry, or another fee-waiver circumstance.
Customers should review recent transactions and report unauthorized card transactions promptly under [Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims](07_disputes_chargebacks_and_fraud_claims.md).

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
2. Types of disputes
| Dispute type | Examples | Typical first step |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Card stolen, card details used online, wallet token compromised | Freeze card and report fraud. |
| Merchant card dispute | Goods not received, defective goods, duplicate charge, cancelled subscription | Contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. |
| ATM dispute | Cash not dispensed, partial dispense, retained card | Report ATM location, date, amount. |
| Direct debit dispute | Wrong amount, no mandate, collected after cancellation | Request direct debit investigation or refund. |
| Bank transfer recall | Payment sent to wrong IBAN or scam recipient | Request recall immediately; recovery not guaranteed. |
| Incoming payment missing | Expected payment not credited | Ask sender for payment proof and trace reference. |
| Fee dispute | Bank fee appears incorrect | Contact customer service with transaction details. |
Different schemes and laws have different deadlines, evidence standards, and refund rules.
