7. ATM cash withdrawals and deposits
Customers can use eligible cards at Aurora ATMs and participating network ATMs. ATM operators may charge their own fees or display conversion options. Aurora Bank does not control fees charged by non-Aurora ATM operators.
ATM services may include cash withdrawal, balance inquiry, PIN change, mini-statement, and cash deposit where available. Cash deposits at ATMs may be subject to counting, verification, counterfeit detection, and delayed availability.
Customers should check the ATM area for tampering, shield the PIN, take receipts, and contact Aurora Bank if the ATM does not dispense cash but the account is debited.

Disputes, Chargebacks & Fraud Claims
6. Time limits
Customers should raise disputes promptly. Card-scheme time limits can be short and may run from transaction date, expected delivery date, cancellation date, or merchant promise date.
Indicative timeframes:
| Claim type | Customer should report by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthorized card transaction | Immediately, and no later than 13 months where legal rules permit | Faster reporting can reduce loss. |
| Goods or services not received | After expected delivery date, usually within 120 days of expected receipt | Scheme rules vary. |
| Refund not processed | After merchant’s refund timeframe, usually within 120 days of refund promise | Evidence needed. |
| ATM cash not dispensed | Within 30 days if possible | ATM balancing may be time-sensitive. |
| Incorrect direct debit | As soon as noticed | Scheme and legal refund rights may apply. |
| Payment sent to wrong account | Immediately | Recovery becomes harder once funds move. |
The exact deadline depends on scheme and legal rules. Aurora Bank may be unable to pursue a claim filed too late.

1. Card types
Aurora Bank may issue the following card types:
| Card type | Linked to | Main purpose | Key restrictions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Debit card | Current account | Spending the customer’s own available funds | No borrowing unless an overdraft is available. |
| Youth debit card | Youth current account | Controlled spending for customers aged 15 to 17 | Lower limits; no gambling merchants; guardian controls may apply. |
| Credit card | Separate credit-card account | Borrowing up to approved credit limit | Interest, minimum payments, and credit checks apply. |
| Virtual card | Current or credit-card account | Online and mobile wallet payments | May not support ATM cash withdrawal. |
| Replacement card | Existing card account | Replaces lost, stolen, damaged, or expired card | Old card may be cancelled when replacement is issued. |
A card remains property of Aurora Bank and must be returned or destroyed on request.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
9. Card payment authorization and settlement
A card transaction usually has two stages:
1. **Authorization**: the merchant requests approval and the available balance is reduced.

1. Payment types supported
Aurora Bank personal accounts may support the following payment types, depending on product eligibility and channel access.
| Payment type | Typical use | Typical currency | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEPA Credit Transfer | Standard euro transfer within SEPA | EUR | Normally arrives by the next business day after execution. |
| SEPA Instant Credit Transfer | Fast euro transfer within participating banks | EUR | Usually processed within seconds, subject to limits and screening. |
| Internal transfer | Transfer between Aurora Bank accounts | EUR or account currency | Usually immediate unless held for checks. |
| Standing order | Repeating customer-initiated payment | EUR | Customer controls amount, recipient, and schedule. |
| Direct debit | Merchant or organization collects payment after customer authorization | EUR | Customer can cancel mandate; merchant contract may remain. |
| International wire | Cross-border transfer outside SEPA or in non-euro currency | Multiple | Additional information, fees, FX spread, and correspondent banks may apply. |
| Card payment | Purchase or withdrawal using debit or credit card | Multiple | Authorization and final settlement may differ. |
Not all payment types are available on youth, savings, basic, or restricted accounts.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
3. Cutoff times
Cutoff times are shown in Central European Time unless otherwise stated. They can change during public holidays, system maintenance, or payment-scheme disruption.
| Payment type | Standard cutoff | Execution expectation |
|---|---:|---|
| SEPA Credit Transfer submitted in online banking | 15:30 on a business day | Sent same business day; usually credited by beneficiary bank by next business day. |
| SEPA Credit Transfer submitted in branch | 14:00 on a business day | Sent same business day if accepted before cutoff. |
| SEPA Instant Credit Transfer | 24/7 where available | Usually within seconds; may fall back or be declined if unavailable. |
| Internal transfer between own Aurora accounts | 24/7 | Usually immediate. |
| Internal transfer to another Aurora customer | 22:00 daily | Usually same day after security checks. |
| International wire in EUR | 13:00 on a business day | Usually 1-2 business days, depending on route. |
| International wire in non-EUR currency | 11:30 on a business day | Usually 2-5 business days, depending on currency and intermediaries. |
| Standing order creation or amendment | 18:00 the business day before due date | Changes after cutoff may apply to the next cycle only. |
| Direct debit cancellation | 18:00 the business day before collection date | Later cancellation may not stop the payment. |
Cutoff times are not promises that the beneficiary will receive funds at a specific hour. Intermediary banks, receiving banks, screening, incorrect details, and payment-system availability may affect timing.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
4. Payment limits
Aurora Bank applies limits to protect customers and comply with law. Limits may vary by product, customer profile, channel, transaction type, and authentication method.
Standard indicative limits for adult personal accounts:
| Channel or payment type | Daily limit | Per-transaction limit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Online SEPA transfer | EUR 25,000 | EUR 15,000 |
| Mobile app SEPA transfer | EUR 10,000 | EUR 5,000 |
| SEPA instant transfer | EUR 5,000 | EUR 2,000 |
| Internal transfer between own accounts | EUR 100,000 | EUR 100,000 |
| ATM cash withdrawal | EUR 600 | EUR 600 |
| Debit card purchase | EUR 5,000 | EUR 3,000 |
| Youth account card purchase | EUR 400 | EUR 200 |
Customers may request a temporary or permanent limit change. Aurora Bank may refuse or reduce limits for security, affordability, account history, product restrictions, or regulatory reasons.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
6. Payment authentication
Payments may require strong customer authentication. Authentication can include a password, app confirmation, biometric confirmation, one-time passcode, hardware token, or call-back verification. Aurora Bank will never ask a customer to disclose a full password, full card PIN, or remote-access code.
Additional security checks may delay a payment. Aurora Bank may hold or reject a payment if fraud, sanctions, money laundering, scam, account takeover, or unusual activity indicators are present.

Contactless payments allow low-value purchases without inserting the card or entering a PIN. Aurora Bank may occasionally require PIN entry or mobile-app confirmation to confirm that the customer still has possession of the card.
Contactless limits vary by country, merchant, and card type. Some merchants may apply lower limits. Offline contactless transactions, such as transport fares, may not appear immediately and can reduce the available balance later.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
10. Secure messages and document upload
Customers should send sensitive information only through approved secure channels. Documents uploaded to online banking should be clear, complete, and unaltered. Aurora Bank may reject documents that are cropped, blurry, password-protected, edited, or inconsistent.
Customers should not send identity documents, card numbers, passwords, or one-time passcodes through ordinary email unless specifically instructed through a secure process.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
1. Security principles
Aurora Bank uses layered security controls to protect accounts. These controls may include encryption, device binding, login monitoring, fraud scoring, strong customer authentication, payment warnings, transaction limits, account locks, and manual review.
Security controls may occasionally delay payments, block card use, restrict online access, or require additional verification. Aurora Bank will not compensate for inconvenience where a control was applied reasonably for safety or legal compliance.

Privacy, Data Protection & Open Banking
8. Data retention
Aurora Bank retains data only as long as necessary for the purpose collected and legal obligations. Indicative retention periods:
| Record type | Typical retention period |
|---|---:|
| Account opening and identity records | 5-10 years after relationship ends, depending on law. |
| Transaction records | 7-10 years after transaction or account closure. |
| Credit applications | Up to 6 years after decision, or longer for active agreements. |
| Complaint records | 5-7 years after closure. |
| Call recordings | 6 months to 7 years depending on call type and legal need. |
| Marketing preferences | Until changed, plus suppression records to honor opt-out. |
| Vulnerability support notes | As long as needed for support and reviewed regularly. |
We may retain data longer where required for litigation, regulatory investigation, fraud prevention, sanctions compliance, or legal hold.

Security, Online Banking & Customer Responsibilities
11. Social media and public channels
Aurora Bank may provide general support through social media but will not conduct full account servicing through public comments. Customers should not post account numbers, card numbers, personal documents, transaction details, or complaint evidence publicly.

retrieved_chunks.content:

11. Cancelling, recalling, or amending a payment
Cancellation rights depend on payment type.
| Payment type | Can the customer cancel? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Future-dated SEPA payment | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before execution. | Online cancellation may be available. |
| Standing order | Usually yes before the cutoff for the next due date. | Cancelling does not cancel contracts with merchants. |
| Direct debit | Usually yes before cutoff on the business day before collection. | Customer should also notify the payee. |
| SEPA instant transfer | Usually no once authorized. | Recall can be attempted but is not guaranteed. |
| Standard SEPA transfer | Recall can be requested after execution. | Recipient bank and recipient consent may be required. |
| International wire | Amendment or recall can be requested. | Fees apply and recovery is not guaranteed. |
| Card purchase | Customer should first contact merchant unless fraud is suspected. | Chargeback may be possible under card scheme rules. |
Aurora Bank cannot guarantee recovery of funds sent to the wrong recipient if the payment was authorized by the customer. The bank may try to contact the receiving bank, but the recipient may need to consent to return funds unless legal rules allow reversal.

Some service providers, payment systems, card schemes, or correspondent banks may process data outside the customer’s country or the EEA. Aurora Bank uses appropriate safeguards where required, such as adequacy decisions, standard contractual clauses, transfer risk assessments, or legal derogations for international payments.
International payments may require sending customer and beneficiary information through correspondent banking networks.

9. Arranged overdrafts
An arranged overdraft is intended as a short-term borrowing facility. It should not be used for long-term borrowing or regular living costs. Aurora Bank may review, reduce, suspend, or cancel an overdraft after notice or immediately where required for risk, fraud, legal, or account-conduct reasons.
Important overdraft rules:
- Interest is charged only on the used arranged overdraft balance.
- The overdraft is repayable on demand.
- Exceeding the limit may lead to declined payments and fees.
- An overdraft limit is not a promise that every payment will be honored.
- Savings accounts and youth accounts do not have overdrafts.
